biography: Born in a quiet Oxfordshire village, Ben Gillias wasn't raised in a motorsport family. His passion ignited during a family trip to Silverstone, captivated by the raw power and precision of Formula 1 cars. He started karting at 14, quickly showcasing a natural talent for racecraft. After winning the local karting championship, Ben entered the Caterham Academy, a breeding ground for future racing stars. A defining moment came during his second Caterham season at Brands Hatch. Starting from the back after a qualifying mishap, Gillias meticulously carved his way through the field, executing daring overtakes and exhibiting remarkable tire management to clinch a stunning victory. This race solidified his reputation as a calculating and resourceful driver. Now at 28, and considered at his peak, Gillias is aiming for a higher motorsport echelon, leveraging his Caterham experience and seeking a seat in a competitive GT racing series, hoping to prove his mettle on a larger stage.
drivingStyle: Gillias is a driver who prioritizes precision and strategy over outright aggression. He's known for his exceptional tire management skills, often coaxing extra laps out of a set while maintaining competitive pace. His corner entry is deliberate, focusing on maximizing exit speed. He rarely makes rash moves, preferring to patiently observe and exploit weaknesses in his opponents' defenses. Under pressure, Gillias remains remarkably composed, making him a formidable competitor in long-distance races where consistency and tactical awareness are paramount.

rivalries.reason: A fierce rivalry developed during their Caterham Academy days. Bellini, an aggressive and flamboyant driver, often clashed with Gillias' more calculated approach, leading to several on-track incidents and heated exchanges off-track.

Jenkins, a rising star in sports car racing, narrowly defeated Gillias in a Caterham endurance event, sparking a rivalry based on mutual respect and a desire to prove who is the better all-around driver.

quirks: Always wears the same faded blue wristband during races.
Listens to classical music to calm his nerves before each session.
Visually inspects his tires, even brand new ones, before getting into the car.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about brute force; it's about understanding the equation and solving it faster than anyone else."
careerHighlight: Winning the Brands Hatch Caterham race after starting last, showcasing his exceptional overtaking skills and tire management.
careerLowPoint: Spinning out on the last lap of a Caterham Academy championship decider while leading, costing him the title.
